title: Accountability, Ownership & Follow-Through
summary: Practice taking responsibility for commitments, communicating status accurately, handling obstacles, and following through on assigned work.
objectives: Explain accountability in a workplace context.
Distinguish ownership from acting outside your authority.
Apply follow-through habits when work changes or obstacles appear.

vocab.def: Responsibility for actions, commitments, decisions, and the accurate communication of results.
Taking appropriate responsibility for work within your role rather than ignoring problems or shifting blame.
Completing agreed actions or communicating clearly when they cannot be completed as expected.
A clear statement about current progress, problems, next steps, or support needed.

sections.heading: Accountability begins with accurate information
sections.body: A worker should not report work as complete when it is unfinished or uncertain. Accurate status reporting helps teams plan and allows problems to be addressed before they become larger.

sections.heading: Ownership does not mean doing everything yourself
sections.body: Taking ownership may mean identifying a problem, documenting it, communicating it, and helping move it toward resolution. It does not mean acting outside your training, authority, or safety limits.

sections.heading: Communicate before a deadline becomes a surprise
sections.body: When a commitment may not be completed on time, early communication gives the team more options. A useful update explains what is complete, what remains, what obstacle exists, and what support or next step is needed.

sections.heading: Follow-through builds trust
sections.body: People remember whether commitments are completed, updates are accurate, and problems are addressed. Reliable follow-through is one of the clearest ways to build workplace trust.

practice.prompt: You realize an assigned task will take longer than expected. What demonstrates accountability?
practice.answer: Communicate the status early, explain what is complete and what remains, and identify a realistic next step or support need.

practice.prompt: You notice a problem that is outside your authority to repair. What does ownership look like?
practice.answer: Communicate or document the problem through the appropriate process and help route it to someone with the proper authority.

quiz.question: Which action best demonstrates accountability?
options: Giving an accurate status update when a commitment may be delayed
Hiding a delay until someone notices
Taking over work outside your authority without asking
quiz.answer: Giving an accurate status update when a commitment may be delayed

lab.objective: Create a workplace status update that accurately describes progress, obstacles, support needed, and next steps.

reflectionPrompt: How can early communication about a problem demonstrate more responsibility than trying to hide or solve everything alone?
